newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian ambassador to return to Iran after row.
newsitem.headline: Australian ambassador to return to Iran after row.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it would return recalled ambassador Stuart Hume to Iran on Friday, although its final reaction to a German court ruling linking Tehran with terrorism remained undecided.
"Stuart Hume will be in Tehran tomorrow," a spokesman for Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer told Reuters.
The spokesman said Hume was returning with instructions to "monitor and assess" the situation there after the German court ruling prompted international condemnation of the Islamic state.
At this stage, he had no particular message for the Iranian government, which the court found to be involved in the 1992 killings of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
"We're still considering things, but we'll have a message at some point," the spokesman said.
Hume was recalled to Australia last Friday to brief the Australian government about the German case.
Australia has been considering its reaction to the ruling, including possible diplomatic and trade sanctions and the withdrawal of an unused line of credit with Tehran.

Downer said on Tuesday he would consider further action against Iran after consultations with key allies, including the United States and European powers, and a detailed examination of the German court verdict.
However, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer moved on Wednesday to reassure farmers that Australia would not cut trade links with Iran.
Australia is exporting up to three million tonnes of wheat to Iran in the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, worth about A$500 million.
